Longitudinal, population-based surveillance of HIV infection and viraemia in the RCCS, July 2013–May 2019, survey rounds 16–19. VL, viral load.
Age and gender profiles of HIV burden in the RCCS, June 2018–May 2019 (round 19). (a) Map of the fishing (triangles) and inland (circles) study communities within the Rakai region in south-central Uganda, produced by using the ggmap package version 3.0.2 [ 52 ] in R (©Stadia Maps ©Stamen Design ©OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributor). (b) Population pyramids in fishing and inland communities. For each 1-year age band, the number of census-eligible individuals (coloured bars) are shown for men (blue) and women (pink). Coloured lines represent smoothed population size estimates. (c) The HIV infection profile is shown in black (line: posterior median estimate, line range: 95% credible interval on the contribution of each 1-year age band to all infections) and values shown on the right y -axis, for both community types (top, bottom) and both genders (left, right). The posterior median estimate of the age range contributing 50% to all infections is visualized as a black horizontal bar for each gender and location. For comparison, HIV seroprevalence within each 1-year age band is shown in orange (bars: posterior median estimates, error bar: 95% credible interval) and values shown on the left y -axis.
Characteristics of populations with and without HIV in the RCCS, June 2018–May 2019, survey round 19.
People with HIV viraemia in the RCCS, from July 2013–January 2015 (round 16) to June 2018–May 2019 (round 19).
Trends in the proportions of PLHIV who have unsuppressed viraemia in the RCCS from July 2013–January 2015 (round 16) to June 2018–May 2019 (round 19). (a) Estimated proportions of people with HIV in 1-year age bands who have unsuppressed viraemia, in men and women of inland communities. On the left, time trends in the proportion of PLHIV with unsuppressed viraemia from round 16 (July 2013–January 2015) to round 19 (June 2018–May 2019) are shown for men and women by 1-year age bands (points: posterior median estimates, line range: 95% Confidence Reference Limits (CrIs)). On the right, posterior median estimates in the proportion of PLHIV with unsuppressed viraemia in round 19 are shown for men and women by 5-year age bands (bars: posterior median estimates, line range: 95% CrIs). The horizontal dotted line represents the 14% suppression threshold implied by the 95–95–95 targets. (b) Same for PLHIV in fishing communities.
Age and gender metrics for people with unsuppressed viraemia in the RCCS from July 2013–January 2015 (round 16) to June 2018–May 2019 (round 19). (a) Estimates for the prevalence of viraemia among PLHIV (median: purple bars, lines: 95% CrI, right y -axis) in each gender and age band are compared with the profile of unsuppressed viraemia (median: black curve, lines: 95% CrI, left y -axis) for inland (top row) and fishing communities (bottom row) in round 19. (b) Time trends in the profile of unsuppressed viraemia for both men and women (facets), coloured by community type (inland or fishing) and survey round (16 or 19) (line: posterior median estimate, ribbon: 95% credible interval). The profiles were multiplied by the population prevalence of viral suppression to visualize shifts in the size of the population exhibiting viraemia.
